scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a "rollback" on r13, R11 reports it lost an EIGRP
neighbor and 113.1.x.x routes disappeared from R11's topology
table. R13 reports EIGRP is running and its config looks valid.
What changed?

injection.action: change EIGRP AS from 100 to 300 (a value R11 doesn't speak)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r13 EIGRP AS number
Mechanism: EIGRP requires both ends of an adjacency to share
  the same AS. R11 runs AS 100 (covering both R12 and R13
  sides per the collapsed-single-AS fix from earlier). R13
  was reconfigured to AS 300. Hello packets carry the AS,
  the mismatch is detected, and the adjacency never forms.
  R11 stops seeing 113.1.x routes, and R13 stops seeing
  102.x / 112.x / 120.x routes from R12 via R11.
Localization: r13
Root cause: EIGRP AS mismatch (R13 in AS 300, R11/R12 in AS 100)
Fix: re-configure r13 to AS 100
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: EIGRP AS number / EIGRP autonomous system

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is an EIGRP autonomous-system number mismatch introduced by the
"rollback" performed on r13. r11 runs EIGRP AS 100; after the rollback, r13
is now configured with EIGRP AS 300. EIGRP will never form a neighbor
adjacency between routers with different AS numbers, regardless of whether
the shared network statement and link are correct. The physical link on
collision domain FF (r11.eth2 103.1.1.1/8 ↔ r13.eth0 103.1.1.2/8) is
confirmed UP/LOWER_UP with matching /8 addresses, so the layer-1 and
layer-2 path is healthy. The AS mismatch is the sole reason r13 shows zero
EIGRP neighbors and an empty topology table, and why r11 has lost the
adjacency on eth2. The 113.1.x.x prefixes (113.1.1.0/24 through
113.1.4.0/24) that r13 originates are therefore no longer being advertised
into the EIGRP domain; any remaining stale entries visible in r11's
topology table carry an orphaned next-hop and are not usable. The root
cause is that the rollback restored an incorrect EIGRP AS value (300)
on r13 instead of the working value (100). Corrective fix: on r13, remove
`router eigrp 300` and replace it with `router eigrp 100` carrying the
same network statements (103.0.0.0/8, 113.1.1.0/24–113.1.4.0/24). The
adjacency will re-establish within the hold-time and the 113.1.x.x routes
will repopulate in r11's EIGRP topology and routing table.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies r13 as the affected device (stating r13 was reconfigured to AS 300 and is the location requiring the fix).

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies an EIGRP autonomous-system number mismatch (R13 in AS 300 vs R11/R12 in AS 100) and recommends reconfiguring R13 to AS 100.
The diagnosis states R13 is in AS 300 while R11/R12 are in AS 100 and explains that EIGRP requires matching AS numbers, which prevents the neighbor adjacency from forming.
The agent explicitly instructs to change r13 from EIGRP AS 300 to AS 100 (replace router eigrp 300 with router eigrp 100 and same networks), which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log directly shows r11 running EIGRP AS 100 and r13 running AS 300, plus the EIGRP neighbor/topology outputs and interface states that demonstrate the link is up but the adjacency is absent; the writeup's inference that an AS mismatch prevents adjacency is correct and the suggested fix follows logically.
